title: Idempotency key client-controlled, unbound to user/command; failed commands marked processed with fabricated success
owner_hint: no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer: Aditya Mandaleeka; component: Ordering.Infrastructure/
rationale: Removes the catch { return default; } in IdentifiedCommandHandler.Handle so inner-command failures propagate: TransactionBehavior's await-using transaction disposes without commit, rolling back the pre-inserted idempotency marker atomically with the failed command — retries re-execute instead of receiving fabricated success. Duplicate-detection semantics untouched; RequestManager untouched. Residual hardening (user binding of ClientRequest) noted as out of scope.
variants_checked: Grep for return default across src confirms this is the only mediator swallow; other catches rethrow correctly; event-publish failure handling is a separate concern.
bypass_considered: Same-key retry after failure now re-executes the real command; fresh-key retry surfaces a genuine 500; cross-user poisoning dropped as unguessable GUIDs (hardening note).
test_note: Handler_throws_when_inner_command_fails in tests/Ordering.UnitTests/Application/IdentifiedCommandHandlerTest.cs asserts propagation and marker creation; rollback is guaranteed by construction (no real-DB test harness exists).
review_reason: The swallow was the defect; removing it restores transactional atomicity at the correct layer with no new surface; the test exercises exactly the modified function in the file's style.
